propositions: Experiment A measures self-consistency of the existing Pass-2/Pass-3 judge by re-judging 50 findings from the G6/E4/T3 cohort with 3 votes each and computing Fleiss' kappa and raw agreement (passes iff kappa>=0.6 AND raw>=0.8), gating R5.

Experiment B measures order-shuffle stability of the gate verdict over plans with >=3 top-level sections, judging each over 3 distinct seeded section-order permutations via the public review_plan entrypoint, gating R3.

Infra-INDETERMINATE verdicts carrying coverage.llm_unavailable or verify_failed are execution failures that are dropped and re-run, while genuine judge-INDETERMINATE outcomes are kept as an agreement category.
E6 makes no src/rebar behavior changes and only measures reliability of the existing gate; it never treats judge output as gold truth, avoiding the circular-adjudication error that invalidated E1.

Experiment A passed with n_findings=50, kappa=0.874, raw_agreement=0.96; Experiment B sub-floored with n_plans=10 of 14 (4 tickets archived after freezing), kappa=0.55, raw=0.70, recorded verbatim as an R3 prerequisite failure.

AC4's hard-coded n_plans>=14 assertion is unsatisfiable because 4 permutable plans' tickets were archived/removed after inputs were frozen, recorded as ticket_not_found excluded rows rather than padded.
